elements.inner_text:
Problem Listen
        Clinical data arise from an informative sampling process, when, which, and how often tests are ordered, yet survival models treat this clinical presence as noise, hurting both accuracy and transportability when practice evolves, discarding the very signal that should inform prediction.
      
      
        Motivation Listen
        
          The same patients present differently under different observation processes; a model overfit to one regime fails when practice shifts.
          The weekend effect, differing test intensity and mortality for weekend vs weekday admissions, offers a controllable shift to stress-test robustness.
          Prior work uses missingness or timing in isolation, not the full observation process jointly with survival.
        
        Clinical presence is signal to model, not noise to ignore.
      
      
        Robustness to Shift
        Transferred (y-axis) vs oracle (x-axis) discrimination under the weekday↔weekend shift, at 1 / 7 / 14-day horizons. Closer to the diagonal = more robust.
        DeepJointFeature stays closest to the diagonal, most robust to the shift; the fine-tuned variant overfits and Feature alone is shift-sensitive.

elements.inner_text:
Method Listen
        
          An LSTM encodes each patient's irregular ICU test sequence into a shared embedding h; three heads then model clinical presence, longitudinal values (Gaussian), missingness (Bernoulli) and timing (cumulative intensity), while a DeepSurv Cox head models survival, all trained jointly.
        
        ℓ(e)=(1−α) ℓS+α ⁣ ⁣∑task∈{L,I,M} ⁣ ⁣wtask(e) ℓtask(e) \ell(e) = (1-\alpha)\,\ell_S + \alpha \!\!\sum_{\text{task}\in\{L,I,M\}}\!\! w_{\text{task}}(e)\,\ell_{\text{task}}(e) ℓ(e)=(1−α)ℓS​+αtask∈{L,I,M}∑​wtask​(e)ℓtask​(e)Joint loss: survival term ℓS plus dynamically-weighted clinical-presence tasks; α balances the two.
        Deep Joint Model: an LSTM embedding h drives the longitudinal (L), inter-observation (I), missingness (M) and survival (S) networks.
      
      
        Headline Numbers
        
          0.878
          C-Index · 1-day horizon · MIMIC-III
          State-of-the-art vs input-matched models
          
            30,834ICU patients
            3presence processes
            1/7/14day horizons

elements.inner_text:
Takeaway Listen
        Explicitly modelling how clinical data are observed, not just their values, yields survival models that are both more accurate and far more transportable when clinical practice shifts. Clinical presence is signal, not noise, and building it into the model is what makes medical predictions transfer across settings, and even flags when the observation process itself has changed.
